Buffalo.wildlife_intro:
Buffalo keeps our crew busy with Norway rats in older blocks, raccoons and squirrels in the canopy neighborhoods, and bats in big older homes each summer. Lake Erie shoreline and Buffalo River  gives wildlife food, water, and cover within a short run of almost every roof in town, and the housing does the rest — once an animal finds a soft soffit, an uncapped chimney, or a gap at the roofline, it treats the house as part of its territory.

The year has a rhythm in Buffalo. Fall pushes squirrels, raccoons, and rodents indoors ahead of winter; spring brings denning mothers looking for chimneys and attic corners; summer is when bat colonies are most visible in older homes and when young animals start ranging on their own. Most Buffalo jobs start with a full roofline and foundation inspection, then removal and sealing every entry we find, because closing only the obvious hole rarely holds.
